svg.text: Idle sawmill: the log saw (row 1) by level: 1, 25 and 50, with circular discs (A) or flat sliding blades (B)
A · Level 1: one disc, four passes
the disc on the far side takes one flat off per pass: forward through it, back, a quarter roll on the belt (orange rollers), four times; the last pass goes on out
A · Level 25: two discs, two passes
a second disc on the near side (half transparent, a spinning blur) cuts the opposite flat in the same pass: two flats per pass, one roll in between
A · Level 50: four discs, one pass
discs above and below too (the bottom one lies in a slot of the belt): all four flats in one pass, no roll
The pass: four flats at once
B · Level 1: one blade, four passes
the plank saw's blade: a flat plate with big teeth that slides back and forth across the trunk, both ends always inside a post (dark slot); it planes the top flat, then the trunk rolls
B · Level 25: two blades, two passes
a second horizontal blade skims the belt under the trunk and takes the bottom flat in the same pass
B · Level 50: four blades, one pass

two vertical blades stand a little further down the line inside the same (wider) portal, in the planes of the far and near flats and slide up and down (lower end in a slit of the belt, upper end in the beam): all four flats in one pass, no roll

A, circular discs (as in the game now): the disc is already drawn and the logic is done. The near and top discs have to be half transparent, or they hide the trunk. The bottom disc is only a rim in the belt.

B, flat blades: one look for both saws, nothing is hidden by a spinning blur, the blades are thin lines that slide. Costs: new drawing for the vertical blades, posts and beam around the trunk (it passes between the posts, like at the plank saw).

Both: the trunk moves at the conveyors' speed, 1 / 2 / 4 tools at levels 1 / 25 / 50 make 4 / 2 / 1 passes (6.9 s, 2.8 s and 0.8 s per trunk). Slabs lie behind the saw. Nothing in the game changes until one is approved.
